thread:
maria: quick question — do we want a single minimal "hosting_manifest" that covers hosted/dedicated/private, or keep three explicit surfaces? thinking about long-term refactors and how clients will pin model versions and routing policies.
chris: +1 to a minimal manifest but we need clear opt-outs. the problem before was hidden fields differing by env and surprises on rollouts.
taylor: agree with chris. core fields I'd expect: model_pin, fallback_stack (list of compatible variants), routing_policy, tenant_isolation (mode), secret_refs. keep vendor-specific extensions in a separate extensions map.
maria: that matches my thinking. main tradeoffs: simpler API for app teams vs surface that exposes too much implementation detail and makes private deployments brittle.
sam: also remember we have Dedicated SLA constraints — the manifest needs a capacity_hint and prewarm flags so runtime can schedule. hosted can ignore capacity_hint but still accept it.
chris: capacity_hint should be advisory. required for Dedicated autoscaler. we should define enum for tenant_isolation: [shared, reserved_gpus, vpc_isolated].
maria: approved. how do we handle auth/secret vs sidecar semantics across environments? Hosted expects control plane-managed secrets, private wants customer KMS/HSM.
taylor: propose secret_refs be schema like: {type: one_of[managed, external], id: string, meta: {kms: optional}}. runtime chooses resolution strategy. no raw secrets in manifest.
maria: sounds good. include an audit field to force export of bindings to logs if customer enables.
sam: routing_policy needs a fallback order — e.g., prefer_low_latency -> prefer_cost -> pinned_model -> fallback_variants. we should encode evaluation order in manifest or let control plane reconcile.
chris: i want a compatibility handshake on connect: runtime and control plane exchange supported_fields, max_seq_len, quant_modes. avoids weird errors at deploy time. simple JSON capability set.
maria: yes — propose a small probe endpoint on startup that returns capability manifest. deploy-bot: deploy-check: probe returned capability_version=1.3, quant_modes=[fp16,int8], max_seq_len=4096.
maria: nice. for rollout safety canary: manifest should include rollout_policy with canary_percent and success_criteria reference (eval set id).
taylor: success_criteria linking to evals is great. avoids surprise quality regressions. also add telemetry_token to manifest for per-model tracing (but token is a secret_ref).
sam: KV cache isolation: private and dedicated might want separate cache namespaces. manifest should include cache_namespace hint to avoid cross-tenant eviction surprises.
maria: good catch. also, on compatibility: we should version the manifest major.minor and support backward compatibility rules in control plane. migrations must be explicit.
chris: ops notes: create e2e test matrix that validates three modes (hosted/dedicated/private) for: model_pin changes, fallback routing, secret resolution, canary rollback. low-effort smoke tests should be part of PR gating.
taylor: devex item: update SDK to expose manifest builder and validation errors early. provide a helpful CLI lint: `redwood manifest lint`.
maria: action items: 1) draft short RFC with proposed schema and handshake probe (I can start). 2) chris to prototype probe response shape. 3) taylor to mock SDK linting. 4) sam to enumerate Dedicated-only fields and mark advisory vs required.
sam: I'll list Dedicated fields by EOD and open a tiny PR with type defs.
chris: I'll sketch the probe example: ```json
{
  "capability_version":"1.0",
  "fields_supported":["model_pin","fallback_stack","routing_policy","secret_refs"],
  "max_seq_len":8192
}
```
maria: perfect. long-term: we should avoid big adapter shims that translate manifest churn — prefer manifest evolution with clear deprecation windows. keep runtime probes lightweight.
taylor: Also recommend a migration runbook: compatibility-check tool, dry-run deploy mode, telemetry gate, and 2-week deprecation periods.
maria: thanks all. filing RFC draft thread now and will @channel when it's up. :rocket:
deploy-bot: RFC draft created: https://redwood.internal/rfc/386-hosting-manifest (status: draft)
maria: pinging for reviews — plz add comments on schema before EOW.
